headline: Ten charged in alleged Hudson Valley cocaine trafficking network
dek: A 153-count indictment accuses defendants from Ulster, Orange and Dutchess counties of coordinating cocaine sales; prosecutors say investigators seized more than a kilogram of cocaine and $12,500 in suspected proceeds.
body: New York prosecutors have charged 10 people in a 153-count indictment alleging that a cocaine distribution network operated across Ulster and Orange counties, with links to Dutchess County. Attorney General Letitia James announced the arrests Wednesday, saying investigators recovered more than one kilogram of cocaine with an estimated street value of about $30,000 and more than $12,500 in cash allegedly tied to drug sales. Nine of the defendants were arraigned in Ulster County Court before Judge Bryan E. Rounds, according to the attorney general's office. News 12 independently reported the same arrest and arraignment totals in its account of the case: https://westchester.news12.com/2026/09/30/10-charged-153-count-indictment-in-alleged-orange-ulster-cocaine-trafficking-ring/2WhHL24JBUEX7l5bebBfZ1.

The investigation began in November 2024 and involved hundreds of hours of physical and covert surveillance, court-authorized cellphone wiretaps, and reviews of phone records and law-enforcement databases, the attorney general's office said. Investigators allege that people in the operation used ordinary food terms, including pizza, pies and water, as coded references to cocaine in text messages and calls. Those details come from the prosecution's account of the investigation and have not been tested at trial.

The indictment describes two related schemes centered on Michael P. Felicello, 51, of Marlboro in Ulster County. Prosecutors allege that Felicello obtained cocaine from several suppliers, including Jorge Lee, Lawrence A. Falcetta Jr. and Michael Brown, and then redistributed it to customers and alleged resellers. The charging document places parts of the alleged activity at a trucking-company parking lot in Orange County, at an Ulster County residence and near a Newburgh deli where one defendant worked. The Times Union described the case as a two-year investigation and likewise reported that the indictment centers on Felicello: https://www.timesunion.com/hudsonvalley/news/article/hudson-valley-cocaine-trafficking-ring-22456168.php.

The other defendants named by the attorney general are Brown, 53, of Newburgh; John J. Dangelo II, 53, of Wallkill; Falcetta, 53, of Marlboro; Deborah A. Foster, 70, of Marlboro; Jose A. Garcia, 57, of Newburgh; Lee, 48, of Marlboro; Joshua A. Mintz, 41, of Highland; Eric S. Oremus, 56, of Poughkeepsie; and Ernesto R. Rodriguez Jr., 25, of Marlboro. Prosecutors allege that the participants occupied different roles in supplying, moving or reselling cocaine. The list of names and hometowns is drawn from the state's release; it is not a finding that any defendant committed the charged conduct.

The attorney general's office also described a March 15 seizure involving Garcia. Investigators allegedly stopped him while he was traveling to supply Brown and seized half an ounce of cocaine; prosecutors say Garcia then returned home within minutes to obtain more cocaine for the order. The release does not establish how the evidence will be challenged in court, and it does not say that every defendant faces every count in the indictment.

The charges include alleged first- and second-degree criminal sale of a controlled substance, third-degree sale and possession counts, and conspiracy. New York's attorney general says a conviction on the top charge, first-degree criminal sale of a controlled substance, carries a maximum sentence of 20 years, although the potential exposure for any individual defendant depends on the counts charged and the outcome of the case. An indictment is a formal accusation, not proof beyond a reasonable doubt.

The case was led by the attorney general's Organized Crime Task Force with the Ulster County Sheriff's Office, the Ulster Regional Gang Enforcement Narcotics Team and the New York State Police Special Investigations Unit. The agencies said the investigation also involved local police, the Ulster County District Attorney's Office and federal Homeland Security Investigations. The defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty. The attorney general's announcement and the independent reports from News 12 and the Times Union did not provide a trial schedule, leaving future court proceedings to determine how the allegations will be tested.
